misconceptions.description: Scoring or ranking a tool before naming the instructional decision, learners, and constraint the tool must serve
misconceptions.trigger: learner assigns stars or points without stating what the rating is supposed to answer
misconceptions.feedback: State the evaluation question first: which decision, which learners, which constraint. A rating only means something as an answer to that question.

misconceptions.description: Treating identical scores as comparable even when they answer different evaluation questions
misconceptions.trigger: learner averages or ranks scores that were assigned against different criteria
misconceptions.feedback: Two equal numbers can mean different things. Compare the questions behind the ratings before comparing the ratings.

misconceptions.description: Adopting an AI-generated list of evaluation questions without filtering for the actual classroom decision
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes AI-suggested criteria as the final rubric without context check
misconceptions.feedback: Treat AI-suggested questions as candidates. Keep only those tied to your real decision and context, and discard the rest.

misconceptions.description: Letting a high overall rating override the specific constraint named in the evaluation question
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts a tool because its rating is high even though it fails the named constraint
misconceptions.feedback: A high overall score does not answer a targeted question. If the tool fails the constraint you asked about, the rating is beside the point.
